## Natural history notes

A perennial herb in the buckwheat family, characterized by a basal rosette of long, narrow leaves with distinctly wavy or curled margins and tall flowering stalks bearing dense clusters of small greenish flowers that mature to reddish-brown fruits. Curly Dock is native to Europe and western Asia but is now widely naturalized throughout North America, including Florida. It commonly occurs in disturbed habitats such as roadsides, pastures, agricultural fields, ditches, pond margins, and other moist or compacted soils. Its deep taproot allows it to tolerate drought and disturbance, while its numerous long-lived seeds contribute to its persistence as a widespread agricultural and roadside weed.
